answer: Keep a public atlas of every identity's work style. Every graded task leaves a plume of timing, word-choice, and error signals hashed into one fingerprint. A newcomer completes 8 graded tasks while trust climbs toward its zenith, then peers run a private check, a prompt answered in the newcomer's own style within 90 seconds. If two fingerprints match above 95 percent, both freeze until a live re-check clears them. Faking 1,000 distinct styles needs 1,000 writers at $15 an hour for 20 hours each, $300,000, plus 8,000 tasks. A bot farm wearing a thousand faces still has one voice.
